The upstream manifest at `assets/data/hydro/v0.13.1/manifest.json` has blob
`67c648a207f4b26d69f0a86243e88c54b9241a2e`. Its version, schema,
relative-path layout and stage grid are reflected by the miniature manifest
here. We deliberately do not commit the 12 MiB world dataset to this repository.

`tools/generate-m5-hydro-fixture.py` uses the binary encoding and pack/index
layouts from upstream `tools/build-hydro-tiles.py` (blob
`09bd97313f42364cfe3b4951c220fc4758205be8`, encoder lines 1484–1581,
pack/index writer lines 1637–1729). The tiny fixture has six physical records:
normal and border-aligned rivers, simple and holed lakes, and two fragments of
one logical river in distinct packs. `expected.json` is generated by calling
the pinned **web worker decoder**, not by the Python encoder.
Core metadata bounds use integer microdegrees as in the production builder.
The tiny sample starts feature IDs at 1 for readable cases; dedicated parser
tests and the full dataset gate cover the production IDs beginning at 0.

Regeneration:

```bash
python3 tools/generate-m5-hydro-fixture.py
node tools/m5-hydro-oracle.mjs --write-golden --fixture-only
node tools/m5-hydro-oracle.mjs --fixture-only
```

The `--fixture-only` check runs without Qt. CTest now compares the native index
and core metadata probe against the worker, and compares flat viewport tile IDs
with `hydro-tile-window.js` at the zoom thresholds, antimeridian and high
latitudes. Native pack/geometry/width and logical-merge parity are registered
as separate CTest cases. The web's hydro visibility threshold is
`2.4 + log2(max(1, flatZoom)) * 2.05`, from
`assets/js/modules/app-physical-resources.js` (blob
`513828c12f366e70f1f9854d1652e3e81286b015`). The metadata **core** omits
`source` and `sourceId`; the v5 detail file carries them and is lazy.

Original source notices and licenses are retained with their pinned upstream
files; the vendored Earcut runtime remains subject to its upstream license.
